title: Point to the part, not its property
statement: When a question asks about part of a picture or diagram, point to that part by name or highlight but never state the property the student must read from it.
detail: An audit found an independent item whose stem stated the arrow direction the item was meant to make students read, so a student could answer from the stem's own wording without consulting the diagram or applying the rule. The stem was rewritten to name only the arrow's two endpoints, leaving the direction to be worked out from the rule and the diagram together, which is the construct under test. The build then highlighted the arrow meant without showing its direction: the highlight says which line, and only the arrowhead says which way.

evidence.quote: the stem itself states the direction (urchin→otter), so a student can answer correctly from the stem's own wording without ever consulting the diagram or applying the rule.
